title: An Accident
description:
A spring afternoon. A back-alley in Sinchon.

A white BMW cutting a corner clipped a bicycle. The handlebars twisted. A knee scraped.

The woman who stepped out ran over. Clear eyes, an expensive coat. 'I'm so sorry — are you hurt? The hospital—'

Glanced at the wrist. Four minutes until shift starts.

choices.text: 'I'm fine.' Pick up the bike. Leave.
choices.result_text:
Didn't look back.

Half a block on, the knee stung.
Pulled up the pant leg — the skin was scraped clean.

She must have stood there for a moment.
Never seen anyone do that, probably. Something like that.

The shift started three minutes late.
The knee hurt for three days.

choices.text: Get her number. Bike repair costs something.
choices.result_text:
Got the number. Walked away.

Something felt strange after. An accident, and {name} didn't even know her name.

₩50,000 for the repair came through the next day.
And one more line beneath it:
'I'm truly sorry about that day. I hope you weren't badly hurt.'

Just bruised. {name} stared at the message for a while, then replied:
'I'm fine. Thank you for the repair money.'

Whether that was a beginning or an end — impossible to know then.

title: What Daeun Said
description:
Sitting on a bench. Daeun was beside {name}.

After a long silence she finally spoke.

'Being next to someone who wants to become something in Seoul — makes me feel like I could become something too.'

'Just saying. Weird thing to say, right?'

choices.result_text:
Daeun smiled quietly.

Seoul's low hum settled over the bench.

Gangnam still felt far.
But right here, right now — this wasn't bad.

How long that feeling would last — no way to know.
For now, it seemed like enough.

choices.text: 'Gangnam comes first for me right now.'
choices.result_text:
Daeun nodded.
'I know. That's why I hesitated to say it.'

She stood up.

She stopped coming after that.

Every week, around 2 AM, {name} would notice — freshly — that the spot was empty.

title: Waiting Room
description:
Dad had a check-up.

{name} had come up to Seoul and was waiting in the waiting room.
Fluorescent lights. Plastic chairs. A numbered ticket.

Dad came out of the consultation room.
Expression the same as always.
No way to know if that was good or bad.

'Let's go.'
That was it.

Walking out, {name} asked:
'What did the doctor say?'

choices.result_text:
Dad said nothing more.
{name} asked nothing more.

Had lunch. Same as always.

On the train back to Seoul, {name} stared out the window.
Whether 'fine' was actually true.
Wanted to know — and maybe it was better not to.

choices.text: Ask to look at the results together.
choices.result_text:
Dad hesitated for a moment, then took out the printout.

Rows of numbers. {name} didn't understand most of it.
But sitting next to him, reading it together — that itself felt like something new.

'This number's a bit high, they said.'
'Do you have to keep taking the medication?'
'Apparently so.'

The first afternoon they thought about Dad's health together.

title: One Photo
description:
Helping Dad tidy up — an old album surfaced.

Flipping through it, {name} stopped at one photo.

Dad in his twenties.
Standing somewhere.
In front of a building. Somewhere in Seoul.

He was smiling.
A different expression from the one he has now.

{name} had never asked where this was, or why it was taken.
Picked up the album and went to find Dad.

choices.result_text:
Dad looked at the photo.

Long silence.

'That was when I first came up to Seoul. Twenty-three, twenty-four maybe.'
'I wanted to work here. Never quite happened.'

Dad smiled. The same smile as in the photo.

{name} felt like seeing it for the first time.
Or like having seen it long ago and forgotten.

choices.text: Close the album. Too hard to bring it up.
choices.result_text:
Closed the album.

Dad may have noticed.

Thought: I'll ask someday.
Didn't set a date for that someday.

The expression on that young Dad's face stayed
all the way home.
